minutes.headline: Committee approved new ELA, math and SEL curricula and authorized an equity audit consultant contract.
minutes.summary: After a long executive session on union negotiations, the committee approved minutes, line-item transfers, curriculum adoptions (math, literacy, Trails SEL), an equity audit consultant, donated sick days, and posting a primary school social worker. It heard presentations on teacher diversification, MTSS, world language, and contingency plans for TCP programs, and gave final approval to the Galapagos trip and policy 122. The business manager reported a one-time DESE payment proposed for a scoreboard, and updated on the primary school AC peer review.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved adoption of new math, literacy and Trails social-emotional curricula, 5-0.
It authorized the superintendent to contract with an equity audit consultant group, 5-0; costs may be split across two fiscal years.
The committee approved line-item transfers, 5-0, moving surplus from substitute and facilities accounts to police detail, contracted services, heating and vehicle lines.
It approved posting a primary school social worker position and transfer of donated sick days, both 5-0.
The business manager reported a one-time, unrestricted state payment for pandemic enrollment loss, proposed for a scoreboard.

why_it_matters: The curriculum grants cover the first years of the math and literacy programs, and administration said it would budget for student consumables from year four, so those costs return to the local school budget later.

The equity audit has no settled funding source yet (this year's budget, next year's professional development or school choice), and the one-time state payment is unrestricted money that must be spent by June 30.
watch_next: Whether the primary school air conditioning project stays in the capital plan that goes to town meeting.
The postponed insecticide bill endorsement, deferred until all members can attend.
